c.tagline: Saudi Arabia's cool mountain summer capital, city of roses and highland resorts.

taxi.fareNote: Street taxis exist but most visitors book through Uber or Careem, which are widely used and often cheaper; agree a fare in advance if using an unmetered street cab.

emergency.note: 999 is police, 997 is the Red Crescent ambulance, 998 is Civil Defense (fire), and 993 reaches traffic police.

hood_desc: The historic heart of the city, home to the restored Shubra Palace museum, the old souks, and the reviving Souq Okaz heritage market; best for first-timers who want landmarks and the old-town feel within reach.

A mountain resort district on Highway 15 famous for the Al Hada cable car (teleferik) down the escarpment, panoramic viewpoints, and hillside hotels; suits travelers who want cooler air, views, and a resort base.
A high village in the surrounding Sarawat mountains (around 2,200-2,500 m) full of fruit gardens, rose farms, and terraced orchards; ideal for a quiet, scenic highland stay and rose-season visits.
A green, family-oriented area in South Ta'if around Al-Rudaf Park, where granite boulders, a lake, and a small zoo draw local families; a calm, leafy base away from the busy center.

water.note: Desalinated tap water is treated but most residents drink bottled; bottled is the safe choice.

transit.hours: City buses and taxis run roughly from early morning until late evening; there is no metro or rail, so ride-hailing apps fill late-night gaps.
transit.note: Ta'if has no metro or tram. Getting around relies on taxis, Uber/Careem, and a limited municipal bus network; the Al Hada cable car is a scenic link rather than a commuter line.
transit.pay: Taxi and ride-hail fares are paid in cash or in-app; there is no rechargeable city transit card. Small notes and coins are useful for street taxis.

bus: SAPTCO intercity coaches to Mecca, Jeddah, Riyadh and Abha
Local municipal buses and shared taxis
train: No passenger rail service to Ta'if

tip.r: Not expected; a service charge is sometimes added, otherwise rounding up or leaving 10-15% for good service is appreciated.

landmarks: Al Hada Mountain and Cable Car
A spectacular 4.2-kilometre cable-car descent from misty Al Hada peak to Al Kar valley, gliding over hairpin bends, baboons and desert cliffs.
Shubra Palace
An elegant early-1900s palace of white latticed balconies blending Hijazi and Ottoman styles, once a royal residence and now Ta'if's regional museum.
Souk Okaz
The revived site of Arabia's most famous pre-Islamic fair, where poetry contests and heritage festivals resurrect 1,500 years of literary tradition.
Ta'if Rose Farms
Terraced gardens that bloom each spring with millions of famed damask roses, distilled in traditional stills into some of the world's priciest rose oil.
Al Shafa Mountain Village
A highland escape above 2,200 metres where fruit orchards, honey stalls and cool mists earn Ta'if its 'City of Roses' summer-resort fame.
Abdullah Ibn Abbas Mosque
A revered mosque marking the burial place of the Prophet's cousin, the great Quranic scholar, anchoring Ta'if's historic centre since the 9th century.
Al Rudaf Park
A beloved natural park where granite boulders, pine groves and resident peacocks make Ta'if's most popular sunset picnic grounds.
Saiysad National Park
A green valley park on the city's outskirts where families gather among acacia trees, walking trails and seasonal wildflower meadows.
Old Ta'if Souq (Souq Al Balad)
The old town's atmospheric market lanes, fragrant with rose water, honey, oud and spices beneath restored Hijazi merchant facades.
Al Kar Tourist Village
A mountain-foot resort at the cable car's base where water parks and terraces overlook the dramatic switchbacks of the Al Hada road.

train.note: Ta'if has no railway station. The nearest rail is the Haramain High Speed Railway (https://www.hhr.sa/), whose closest stops are Makkah and Jeddah, about 1.25 to 2 hours away by road, while Saudi Arabia Railways (https://www.sar.com.sa/) serves only the centre and east of the country. A branch line up the escarpment to Ta'if has been discussed for years but is not built, and Saudi Arabia has no international passenger trains, so arrivals are by air, coach or car.

bus.note: SAPTCO (https://www.saptco.com.sa/) runs frequent coaches from the Ta'if bus station to Jeddah (about 2-2.5 hours), Makkah (roughly 1.25 hours), Riyadh (about 9 hours) and south towards Abha; tickets are sold at the counter and in the SAPTCO app. Non-Muslim travellers must not pass through Makkah - coming from Jeddah the road turns off onto the 'Christian bypass' short of the holy city and climbs the escarpment in switchbacks to Ta'if, so check that your service uses that route. SAPTCO's international coaches to the Gulf states, Jordan and Egypt run from Riyadh, Jeddah or Dammam rather than from Ta'if.

ferry.note: Ta'if sits at about 1,900 m in the Sarawat mountains, well inland; the nearest passenger sailings are Red Sea crossings from Jeddah and Duba towards Egypt and Sudan, several hours away by road, and those services are frequently suspended.

half.name: As-Sail Al-Kabir
half.blurb: Valley town along the old mountain road down from Ta'if, known for its date palms and seasonal flash floods.

full.name: Jeddah
full.blurb: Red Sea port city with a historic old town of coral-stone buildings and a long waterfront corniche.

full.name: Al Baha
full.blurb: Cooler mountain region known for juniper forests and stone villages terraced into the Sarawat range.
